reflection: The notebook shows that most single-factor gains are small and unstable: nearly every R1 factor helped in 2-3 years and failed in 2024 or 2022, so the average gain stayed below 0.010. The strongest existing signals are Apple's own volatility and MSFT's one-day return, so the more promising route is to keep those signals but make them less sensitive to regime changes. Several near-copies and ratios of Apple volatility were redundant (similarity 0.72-0.95), so this round I want new information from gaps, market trend and relative-volatility scaling. I will also try pairs where one factor is a relative move and the other a peer lead, since the notebook shows neither role has worked alone.

lessons.name: aapl_vol10_to_vol60_ratio
lessons.lesson: The ratio of short to long Apple volatility mostly restated AAPL_volatility_10d (similarity 0.72), and its regime-dependent sign flipped between 2022 and 2023, so it added no stable new information.

lessons.name: msft_return_1d_zscore20
lessons.lesson: Standardizing MSFT's one-day return made it a near-copy of MSFT_return_1d (0.95) and it helped only Random Forest and missed in 2024, so the extra scaling did not add robust signal.

lessons.name: qqq_range_10d_mean
lessons.lesson: A 10-day average of QQQ's high-low range is a slow volatility proxy that overlapped with existing volatility factors and was dominated by the 2024 regime shift.

lessons.name: aapl_close_location_3d
lessons.lesson: The 3-day average position of Apple's close within its daily range is noisy and mostly tracks the existing 3-day mean return, so it fails in most years.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_msft_cum_5d
lessons.lesson: The 5-day Apple-minus-MSFT spread is highly similar to AAPL_cum_return_5d (0.54) and carries no consistent next-day signal across years.

lessons.name: peer_disagreement_5d_mean
lessons.lesson: Average absolute gap between NVDA and MSFT returns is a regime indicator that spiked in 2024 and was not directionally informative for Apple's next close.

factors.name: msft_return_1d_sign
factors.hypothesis: MSFT_return_1d is driven by a few large moves that differ across years (it failed in 2024 when the magnitudes were extreme); using only the direction of MSFT's last-day move should keep its useful lead signal while removing outlier sensitivity.

factors.name: aapl_vol10_relative_qqq
factors.hypothesis: Apple's 10-day volatility alone reflects both market-wide and idiosyncratic regimes; dividing by QQQ's 10-day volatility isolates Apple-specific risk, which should hold up in years when the whole tech market is volatile (such as 2022 and 2025).

factors.name: aapl_overnight_gap_1d
factors.hypothesis: The overnight gap (open relative to the previous close) captures after-hours news flow that is not in the close-to-close returns already in the set, so it may carry partly independent next-day information.

factors.name: qqq_close_to_ma20
factors.hypothesis: The position of QQQ relative to its 20-day average describes the market trend regime; the existing factors only cover Apple's own trend, so this adds a market-wide trend state that may help in trending years like 2023 and 2024.

factors.name: aapl_minus_nvda_mean_5d
factors.hypothesis: NVDA_cum_return_5d is a peer-lead signal that is strong in some years; averaging Apple's daily gap to NVDA over five days measures whether Apple is lagging or leading the AI-driven peer, which should complement NVDA's momentum rather than repeat it.

factors.name: qqq_return_z_10d
factors.hypothesis: AAPL_volatility_10d describes Apple's own risk state; a volatility-scaled QQQ return shows whether the market's latest move is unusually large relative to its recent noise, which is a peer lead that should work jointly with Apple's volatility regime.
